title: Preventing P-Trap Siphonage with Proper Venting
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block dangerous sewer gases from entering living spaces. A frequent issue in drainage systems is trap siphonage, which occurs when negative air pressure pulls the water seal out of the trap as waste flows down the drain arm. To prevent self-siphonage, the trap arm must maintain an adequate slope and connect to a properly sized vent pipe before exceeding maximum unvented length limits specified by local code. Proper venting equalizes atmospheric pressure, protecting the trap water seal every time a fixture discharges.

Preventing P-Trap Siphonage with Proper Venting

A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block dangerous sewer gases from entering living spaces. A frequent issue in drainage systems is trap siphonage, which occurs when negative air pressure pulls the water seal out of the trap as waste flows down the drain arm. To prevent self-siphonage, the trap arm must maintain an adequate slope and connect to a properly sized vent pipe before exceeding maximum unvented length limits specified by local code. Proper venting equalizes atmospheric pressure, protecting the trap water seal every time a fixture discharges.
